notes: Port of crypto-autoresearcher research/cryptographic_assumption_attack_corpus_20261101 (commit 004355570fa983535696439b1781cb762dae3607) into this schema. The five frozen targets carry the sibling repository's kernel-checked theorem names; their Lean files live in the sibling, so no formal block is recorded here and their status stays proved_internal_unreviewed for this corpus even though the sibling's five semantic attestations returned 'holds'. Queue items are open obligations. Cross-links attach each item to the ECDLP claims whose stated assumptions it touches; the xedni conditional-hazard recurrence, previously free text in OBSTRUCTION-XEDNI-HEIGHT, is promoted to a node.

Theorem names: ModAlias.modulus_alias_and_bounded_repair, SubgroupMembership.ambient_membership_does_not_imply_designated_subgroup, AdaptiveBatching.adaptive_rlc_cancellation, PolynomialFunctionAlias.nonzero_polynomial_zero_function, SchnorrSpecialSoundness.extract_of_distinct_challenges (namespace CryptoResearch.AttackCorpus). nodes.label: 'Equality in ZMod q is equality of the represented integers'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: equality of two values after casting into ZMod q proves equality of the integers they represent.
nodes.scope: Refuted by 0 and q. The corrected statement needs a canonical range (a, b < q, q > 0); signed and multi-limb encodings need their own range theorem.

nodes.label: Modulus alias and bounded repair (Lean, sibling)
nodes.statement: For q > 0 the integers 0 and q are distinct but equal in ZMod q; if a, b < q and their casts agree then a = b.
nodes.scope: Arithmetic alias only. Calling a circuit vulnerable needs a source-to-constraint refinement showing the range check is absent.
assumptions: Canonical range a, b < q for the repair

nodes.label: 'An accepted ambient group element is a scalar multiple in the intended subgroup'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: any element accepted as a valid ambient group element can be treated as lying in the designated order-q subgroup.
nodes.scope: Refuted by a product-group countermodel; the repair needs an exact-order generator and a membership witness or proven cofactor-clearing projection, and protocols may also need nonidentity.

nodes.label: Ambient membership does not imply designated-subgroup membership (Lean, sibling)
nodes.statement: In ZMod 2 x ZMod 3 with designated subgroup s -> (0, s), the element (1, 0) is a valid ambient element outside the subgroup with additive order 2; an exact-order-q generator induces an injective scalar map from ZMod q.
nodes.scope: Abstract product group, not a curve equation: it refutes the group-theoretic inference, not any implementation. Decoding, on-curve checks and twist handling are separate interfaces.
assumptions: Designated subgroup given by an exact-order generator

nodes.label: 'Random-linear-combination batching fails with probability <= d/|F| even against adaptive errors'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: an RLC batch check has failure probability at most d/|F| even when the invalid terms may depend on the challenge.
nodes.scope: Refuted by e0(rho) = -rho, e1(rho) = 1. The d/|F| bound holds only for errors fixed before an independent uniform challenge.

nodes.label: Adaptive RLC cancellation and fixed-error count (Lean, sibling)
nodes.statement: Challenge-dependent errors cancel for every challenge; for errors fixed in advance whose coefficient polynomial is nonzero of degree <= d over a field, at most d challenges accept.
nodes.scope: Counting statement. Uniform sampling (the PMF step) and Fiat-Shamir transcript semantics are outside the theorem.
assumptions: Nonzero coefficient polynomial of degree <= d

nodes.label: 'Polynomials equal at every field point are equal as formal polynomials'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: two polynomials over F_q that agree as functions on F_q are equal as formal polynomials.
nodes.scope: Refuted by X^q - X. True below degree |F| in one variable; multivariate statements need an individual-degree or total-degree bound for the evaluation domain.

nodes.label: Nonzero polynomial with zero function (Lean, sibling)
nodes.statement: X^q - X is nonzero and vanishes at every element of F_q; a univariate polynomial of degree < |F| vanishing on all of F is zero.
nodes.scope: Field fact. Binding it to a commitment's degree bound, quotient relation and SRS is a separate refinement.

nodes.label: 'Any two accepting Schnorr-like transcripts reveal the witness'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: two accepting transcripts of a Schnorr-like protocol always yield the witness.
nodes.scope: Refuted by two transcripts with the same challenge, and over ZMod 4 by a nonunit challenge difference such as 2.

nodes.label: Schnorr extraction countermodels: equal challenges; nonunit difference over ZMod 4
nodes.statement: Two accepting transcripts with equal challenges give no invertible difference; over ZMod 4 the nonzero difference 2 is not a unit, so (s - s')/(e - e') is undefined.
nodes.scope: Stated in the corpus README. The audited Lean declaration is the positive theorem, so these countermodels are not themselves kernel-checked.

nodes.label: Schnorr special soundness under exact fork hypotheses (Lean, sibling)
nodes.statement: In an exact prime-order subgroup, two accepting transcripts with the same commitment and distinct challenges satisfy w = (s - s')/(e - e') in the scalar field.
nodes.scope: Special soundness only: not a proof of knowledge, a Fiat-Shamir theorem, or a discrete-log reduction. Producing the fork is a separate model-relative step.

nodes.label: Fiat-Shamir-derived batching challenges act as independent uniform challenges
nodes.statement: A batching coefficient derived by hashing the transcript behaves, for the purpose of the fixed-error bound, like a challenge sampled independently after the errors are fixed.
nodes.scope: The corpus calls this an unconnected interface: it needs a transcript-binding theorem (all committed values absorbed before the challenge) and a ROM or concrete hash argument.
assumptions: Transcript binds every term the adversary chooses

nodes.label: Fiat-Shamir RLC batch verification fails with probability <= d/|F|
nodes.statement: Deployed batch verification with a Fiat-Shamir-derived combination coefficient inherits the d/|F| fixed-error bound.
nodes.scope: Holds only through the fixed-error count plus challenge independence plus a canonical transcript encoding; the protocol corpus has not discharged the last two.

nodes.label: Adaptive xedni trials satisfy a history-uniform conditional-hazard recurrence
nodes.statement: Conditioned on any history of failed xedni trials, the next trial succeeds with probability at most the one-shot bound, so the waiting time is at least geometric with that rate.
nodes.scope: Promoted from free text in OBSTRUCTION-XEDNI-HEIGHT's assumption list. A one-shot bound alone does not imply it: fully correlated trials and adaptive lift selection are countermodels to the inference (protocol corpus ONE-SHOT-REPEAT).
assumptions: Trials may adapt lifts to earlier failures

nodes.label: One-shot success bound versus geometric waiting time
nodes.statement: Formalise that a one-shot bound does not imply a geometric expected waiting time (correlated and adaptive-history countermodels), and the repair: a uniform conditional-hazard recurrence implies the bound.
nodes.scope: Priority 0 queue. The sibling JKSST finite audit covers part of it; the xedni-specific instance is ASM-XEDNI-HAZARD-RECURRENCE.

nodes.label: Cofactor clearing as a uniform projection
nodes.statement: Give the exact kernel, image and pushforward count of cofactor clearing, and product-group countermodels when factors share divisors or the assumed decomposition fails.

nodes.label: 'Special soundness implies Fiat-Shamir security'
nodes.statement: Formalise the constant-hash countermodel (challenge always zero, choose R = sG) and isolate the domain-separation and random-oracle programmability premises a Fiat-Shamir theorem needs.

nodes.label: 'Independent generators' read as literal linear independence
nodes.statement: Exhibit the scalar-relation kernel and alternate openings when a generator relation is known, and state binding as computational (reducing to DLP) rather than linear independence in a cyclic group.
nodes.scope: Priority 0 queue; classification false-as-stated / open assumption.

nodes.label: Completeness, zero knowledge, soundness and proof of knowledge are distinct
nodes.statement: Formalise the always-accept protocol (complete and perfectly zero knowledge but unsound) and keep HVZK and malicious-verifier definitions separate.

nodes.label: DLP, CDH and DDH are not interchangeable
nodes.statement: Record reduction direction formally and give an abstract oracle model in which DDH is easy while the computational problems remain assumptions.
nodes.scope: Priority 0 queue; classification model-relative / open assumption. Matches this corpus's fixed reduction direction (CDH reduces_to DLP).

nodes.label: Exceptional cases of elliptic-curve addition formulas
nodes.statement: Prove the domain of affine and projective addition formulas, exhibit exceptional denominators, and refine complete formulas to the abstract group law.

nodes.label: Invalid-curve and twist input paths
nodes.statement: Bind byte decoding, curve membership, subgroup membership, nonidentity and error handling to the protocol model.

nodes.label: Fiat-Shamir transcript encoding
nodes.statement: Prove injective canonical serialisation with statement and public-input absorption, protocol and domain tags and length separation; exhibit concatenation collisions when any is omitted.

nodes.label: KZG trapdoor and degree boundaries
nodes.statement: With known tau and z != tau, the KZG scalar equation admits a forged proof proportional to (c - y)/(tau - z); state this algebraic failure separately from q-SDH and SRS security and freeze degree, subgroup and setup premises.

nodes.label: KZG batch opening boundaries
nodes.statement: Audit duplicate evaluation points, vanishing denominators, adaptivity to batching challenges and the exact nonzero-polynomial bound in KZG batch openings.

nodes.label: PLONK permutation and lookup product premises
nodes.statement: Make every nonzero-denominator, challenge-timing, domain-size, degree and boundary-row premise of the permutation and lookup arguments explicit, and search small fields for collisions first.

nodes.label: In-circuit elliptic-curve arithmetic refinement
nodes.statement: Relate limb and range constraints and incomplete formulas in circuits to native curve operations and subgroup policy.

nodes.label: ECDLP random self-reducibility over the exact subgroup
nodes.statement: Prove the exact-subgroup permutation and success preservation of the blinding map, without randomising over the full curve group.

nodes.label: Separate rho correctness, collision time and collision usefulness
nodes.statement: Separate deterministic collision correctness from the random-map collision-time model and from the probability that a collision is useful.

nodes.label: Hash-to-curve contracts (RFC 9380)
nodes.statement: Bind domain separation, map suite, cofactor clearing, uniform or nonuniform designation, subgroup output and exceptional cases to RFC 9380 instead of a generic 'hash is random' premise.

nodes.label: Concrete and multi-user security accounting
nodes.statement: Track query counts, loss factors, constants, union bounds and correlated users instead of an asymptotic adjective.

nodes.label: Generic-group lower bounds versus transparent encodings
nodes.statement: Prove a transparent-encoding countermodel to 'all algorithms' wording, then formalise the random-injective-encoding oracle and collision transcript that Shoup's theorem actually covers.

nodes.label: Finite random-oracle game semantics for the forking lemma
nodes.statement: Build finite ROM game semantics with query indexing, replay, aborts, distinct challenges and exact probability loss.

nodes.label: ROM, AGM, KEA, q-SDH and QROM as named models
nodes.statement: Treat each as a named model or assumption and prove reductions between formal games, never recast as unconditional algebra.

nodes.label: SNARK definitions as separate games
nodes.statement: Formalise completeness, knowledge soundness, zero knowledge, simulation soundness and adaptive variants as different games before treating 'secure SNARK' as one predicate.

nodes.label: End-to-end KZG, Groth16 and PLONK
nodes.statement: Full commitment and SNARK theorems need pairings, polynomial-commitment interfaces, CRS/SRS semantics, encodings and game proofs beyond the first-wave algebraic controls.

nodes.label: Curve-selection assumptions with exact curve and subgroup identities
nodes.statement: Audit MOV/Frey-Rueck embedding degree, anomalous and supersingular exclusions, twists, cofactors and endomorphism claims with exact curve and subgroup identities.

edges.statement: 0 and q are distinct integers with equal casts into ZMod q.
(1, 0) in ZMod 2 x ZMod 3 is ambient-valid and outside the designated order-3 subgroup.
e0(rho) = -rho, e1(rho) = 1 cancels for every challenge.
X^q - X is nonzero and vanishes on F_q.
Equal challenges, or a nonunit difference over ZMod 4, give no extraction.

The forking reduction's assumption 'obtains two related accepting transcripts' is used through this extraction step; its hypotheses (same commitment, distinct challenges, prime order) are what the fork must deliver.
The reduction's 'correct subgroup validation' assumption is a separate membership check: ambient validity does not supply it.
Special soundness alone does not give Fiat-Shamir security; the random-oracle and domain-separation premises carry the reduction.
No machine-checked forking lemma yet connects the Lean extraction theorem to the ROM reduction's loss.
The abstract form of the invalid-curve boundary: accepting an ambient element does not place it in the prime subgroup.
Decoding, on-curve, subgroup and nonidentity checks are not yet bound to a protocol model.
SEC 1 lists on-curve, public-key, subgroup, order and nonidentity validation as separate checks; the corpus treats each as its own interface.
Blinding must randomise inside the exact prime subgroup; randomising over the full curve group breaks success preservation.
An instance outside the designated subgroup is not a valid input to the prime-order self-reduction.
Cofactor clearing is a uniform projection onto the prime subgroup only under the group-structure and coprimality hypotheses the queue item makes explicit.
Cofactor-based ECDH arguments need the exact kernel/image count of cofactor clearing.
CDH hardness is an assumption separate from DLP hardness; only the direction CDH reduces_to DLP is a theorem.
The converse direction (DLP from CDH) holds only conditionally, through auxiliary-curve constructions.
The lower bound is for random injective encodings; a transparent encoding makes 'all algorithms' wording false.
'BSGS is optimal by Shoup' holds only among generic algorithms.
AGM equivalences are model-relative and require algebraic representations.
Transferring AGM results to the GGM is itself a model bridge to be proved, not assumed.
The random-mapping heuristic is the collision-time layer only; correctness and usefulness of a collision are separate statements.
Each exclusion must be audited with exact curve and subgroup identities.
The waiting-time step needs each adaptive trial's marginal success probability to stay O(1/p); by THM-HAZARD-MARGINAL-SUFFICES this replaces the hazard recurrence previously listed as free text.
Correlated and adaptive-history countermodels show the one-shot bound alone does not yield the recurrence.
The fixed-error count is the algebraic core of the batch bound.
The fixed-error count applies only if the derived challenge acts as independent of the errors.
Without a canonical transcript encoding the adversary may choose terms after the challenge is fixed.
KZG batch openings add duplicate-point and vanishing-denominator premises to the generic batch bound.
The true/fake fall-degree gap is the formal-versus-function gap: each X_j^2 + X_j vanishes as a function on F_2 but not formally, which is why reducing modulo the field equations changes the degree.
Pedersen and IPA binding is computational: a known generator relation (a discrete logarithm) gives alternate openings.
Multi-user security must account for amortised multi-target attacks rather than per-key asymptotics.
Hash-to-curve output lands in the prime subgroup only after the suite's cofactor clearing.

research_targets.label: Discharge or break the xedni conditional-hazard recurrence
research_targets.objective: Decide whether adaptive xedni trials satisfy a history-uniform conditional-hazard bound. A countermodel with adaptive lift selection would leave OBSTRUCTION-XEDNI-HEIGHT without its waiting-time conclusion; a proof for the selected-lift process closes that bridge.
research_targets.acceptance: A Lean theorem: either the recurrence for the JKSST trial process under stated lift-selection rules, or an explicit adaptive process meeting every other JKSST hypothesis whose waiting time violates the geometric bound.
research_targets.next_step: Formalise the generic separation (one-shot bound without geometric waiting time) from the protocol corpus, then specialise it to the JKSST selected-lift process.

research_targets.label: Protocol-layer Priority 0 queue
research_targets.objective: Discharge the six Priority 0 items after the frozen five, each with counterexample and repair in one module.
research_targets.acceptance: The sibling corpus's acceptance rules: matching quantifier order, premises satisfied by the countermodel, every used hypothesis exposed, axiom audit clean, independent semantic review.
research_targets.next_step: Freeze target YAMLs in crypto-autoresearcher formal/targets/ for COFACTOR and FS-ZERO-HASH.
